title: Jury convicts Rodney Hinton of all charges in death of retired deputy Larry Henderson

 CINCINNATI (WKRC) — A Hamilton County jury found Rodney Hinton Jr. guilty on all charges Friday in the death of retired sheriff’s deputy Larry Henderson, rejecting Hinton’s insanity defense after more than two days of deliberations.
 Jurors convicted Hinton of murder, felonious assault and reckless homicide. He was immediately taken into custody following the verdict and is scheduled to be sentenced at 9 a.m. Nov. 16. 
 Henderson was working a special traffic detail for the University of Cincinnati’s graduation on May 2, 2025, when Hinton struck him with a vehicle. Henderson died from his injuries.
 The crash happened hours after Cincinnati police showed Hinton body-camera video from the shooting death of his son, Ryan Hinton. The defense argued Hinton was legally insane at the time of the crash, while prosecutors maintained he intentionally drove at Henderson. 
 View post on X 
 The case went to the jury after a 10-day trial that centered on Hinton’s mental state and whether he acted purposely. 
 Hinton's attorney Clyde Bennett spoke about Hinton's family after the verdict was read.
 "They're pleased that his life was spared. They're pleased that he won't be in prison for the rest of his life without the possibility of parole. But they're disappointed that he has to be sentenced to 15 years of life. So we're disappointed."
 Sheriff Charmaine McGuffey said she and her staff can't be happy about the verdict but they are satisfied. 
 "Him taking Larry's life affected so many people, including his people, including him. It's a tragedy but it's a tragedy of his own making. She went on to say, "We can all now grieve and move forward with some finality."
 Bennett said they'll appeal.
